_about: Parameters for the pre-OPT backend sponsor-tiers recipe, proposed by the assistant and NOT yet confirmed by the author. Each has a value and one sentence of reasoning. None is a measured fact, and none was tuned against the sample run's outcome.

days_per_month.why: Average Gregorian month (365.25 / 12), used only to express day differences as months.

max_vintage_age_months.why: Funding recency and filing history go stale and the book calls the record a rear-view mirror; six months is a planning default with no test behind it.

funding_window_months.why: Two years back from the data's own newest funding date keeps the discovery pool to companies that raised money recently in the data; it is a heuristic for 'may be hiring', not a tested predictor.

proven.why: Ten reported approvals so one filing or a duplicated count cannot carry the top tier (every count in the file is even, cause undocumented), and 90 percent so a visible denial history keeps a company out; p is the chapter 11 worked-example value for Proven, not a calibrated probability.

likely.why: Four reported approvals is still at least two if the even counts are double-counted, and 70 percent tolerates some denials; p is the chapter 11 worked-example value for Likely.

thin.why: A matching title exists but the counts or rate fall below Likely; 0.3 is an ordinal placeholder chosen so the scorer files the row under Skip for any timeline factor, not a probability.
